papers.title: Closure of Traceful Radiation-Gauge Reconstruction with Matter: General Kerr Conditions, a Thin-Shell Benchmark, and a Conserved Torus
papers.abstract: We formulate the closure problem for first-order, traceful radiation-gauge metric reconstruction on a Kerr background with matter. The reconstruction is decomposed into Weyl-curvature, Ricci-trace, and mass--angular-momentum completion sectors. For compatible initial, gauge, and completion data, we establish local existence and uniqueness of the resulting triangular transport system on a regular Kerr domain, and identify the additional conditions needed for a closed global formulation. This is not a global existence theorem. We test the framework using two conserved matter sources. For a thin shell around a Schwarzschild black hole, Israel matching, regularity, asymptotic flatness, a barotropic equation of state, and fixed rest mass determine the static, axial, and leading rotational sectors. The ADM-mass shift is $\sqrt{1-2M/R}$ times the shell rest mass, while the axial sector determines the angular momentum, moment of inertia, and interior frame dragging. We also construct a stationary constant-angular-momentum fluid torus on Kerr and compute its Newman--Penrose Ricci projections, showing that nonspherical sources generally excite coupled Ricci sectors. The shell provides a closed benchmark, while the torus illustrates the additional structure required for general Kerr sources.

papers.title: Can a Wormhole Induce a Monopole?
papers.abstract: Could a star orbiting one mouth of a wormhole make the mass seen near the other rise and fall? We show that the periodic mass change proposed for searches around Sgr A* does not occur. The predicted signal comes from treating static solutions with different masses as successive states of the same orbiting system. In the Maxwell analogue, charge measured around a mouth changes only when current crosses the measuring surface. Similarly, in gravity, source motion cannot change the observed Schwarzschild mass at first order. Furthermore, the Bondi mass of a vacuum observer end cannot increase even beyond first order, though gravitational radiation can reduce it. The same observer-side dynamics can be reproduced with both mouths in one exterior at sufficiently large separation.

papers.title: First-order corrections to equatorial periodic orbits around rapidly rotating black holes in dynamical Chern--Simons gravity
papers.abstract: We calculate first-order corrections to the energy, radial period, and circumferential turning radii of equatorial periodic orbits around rapidly rotating black holes in dynamical Chern--Simons (dCS) gravity. Using an analytic fit to the metric correction, we match each orbit to a Kerr reference at fixed dimensionless spin, dimensionless specific angular momentum, and rational periodicity. The period correction combines a direct contribution at fixed energy with compensation from the energy adjustment that preserves periodicity. Their competition produces sign changes across orbital families and reference paths. In a two-parameter scan, negative period corrections are dominated by energy compensation for sampled prograde orbits and by the direct contribution for sampled retrograde orbits. We locate $C_T=0$ boundaries, where the coefficient of the first-order fractional period correction vanishes. Circumferential shifts can differ in sign from coordinate shifts. Numerical kludge waveforms at leading quadrupole order and their discrete spectra connect these corrections to phase accumulation and harmonic frequency shifts. At fixed dimensionless orbital parameters and physical mass of the small body, this phase contribution can be reproduced to first order by rescaling the Kerr mass. For the $C_T=0$ orbit examined here, this contribution is suppressed at equal black hole masses, while corrections to the waveform and spectral amplitudes remain nonzero.

papers.title: Field-level modeling of halo and galaxy alignments
papers.abstract: We develop an effective field theory (EFT) of intrinsic alignments at the level of spin-2 field fluctuations of large-scale structure tracers, such as the shapes of galaxies and dark matter halos. Our perturbative model includes the non-linear treatment of the Zel'dovich displacement, and contains all necessary shape operators through the third order. We apply our field-level model to the full 3D distribution of galaxy shapes, whose sky projections are a known contaminant of cosmic shear measurements. Our field-level EFT model achieves a better description of the helicity fields of dark matter halo shapes than the standard non-linear alignment (NLA) and tidal torquing + tidal alignment (TATT) models in the literature, as evidenced by improved correlations with the simulations' initial conditions. We perform precision measurements of field-level bias parameters by means of a generalized least-squares problem, for which we derive an optimal estimator and analytic covariance matrices. We measure the full set of linear, quadratic, and cubic shape bias coefficients as a function of halo mass in the $\texttt{Quijote}$ N-body simulations. We then study the intrinsic alignments of galaxies in the $\texttt{FLAMINGO}$ hydrodynamical simulation, focusing on observationally relevant samples: spirals, ellipticals, luminous red galaxies (LRG) and emission-line galaxies (ELG). We detect linear and nonlinear alignment coefficients at high significance for LRG, spiral and elliptical galaxies. We also find evidence for non-zero density-weighted tidal bias coefficient of the simulated ELG. This work supports the notion that EFT-based models of alignments will be paramount in optimally extracting constraints from future shape correlations, and lays the foundation for the development of simulation-based priors for future galaxy shape samples.

papers.title: Attractors and initial-condition sensitivity in Horndeski cosmologies
papers.abstract: We study whether nearby homogeneous cosmological histories approach or move away from the Genesis and contracting solutions. We also determine how an uncertainty in the scalar velocity at a later stage affects the inferred initial velocity. In the Genesis models, including the gravitational dynamics can substantially change this relation. We find that convergence of homogeneous solutions can occur even around backgrounds with unstable perturbations, and therefore attraction of the background is not sufficient to establish that a cosmological solution is physically viable. In the contracting model, one power-law solution attracts nearby trajectories, whereas another repels them. The strength of these effects depends on how the cosmological state is parametrized. Their evolution through the subsequent bounce is not considered here.

papers.title: Semi-agnostic inspiral modeling: the massless scalar case at leading post-Newtonian order
papers.abstract: We introduce a semi-agnostic modeling framework for black hole binary inspirals beyond general relativity that fixes the field content without selecting a particular theory. We expand in the post-Newtonian order and in powers of $l/L$, where $l$ is the characteristic length-scale that controls deviations from General Relativity and $L$ is the characteristic length-scale of the system. We focus on the case of a massless scalar field coupled with the metric, at leading post-Newtonian order. Taking into account the scaling with $l/L$ of both the interaction terms and the quantities that characterise the sources, we find that the inspiral can be described in terms of a small number of universal parameters. Such a parametrisation is suitable for obtaining combined bounds from multiple sources and performing searches for specific fields.

papers.title: Two-dimensional galaxy cluster shapes using lensing data: a simulated analysis
papers.abstract: Context. Cluster morphology reflects assembly history and dynamical state. High-resolution weak lensing can reveal departures from spherical symmetry, but its ability to recover two-dimensional shapes remains less explored. Aims. We assess how reliably weak lensing recovers projected cluster morphology and its dependence on orientation and dynamical state. We also compare large-scale weak-lensing morphology with that traced by strong lensing near the cluster centre. Methods. We study three clusters at $z=0.22$ from The Three Hundred Project, representing relaxed, mildly disturbed and unrelaxed systems. For each, we consider three random projections and three along the principal axes of the mass tensor. For each projection, we generate 128 weak-lensing catalogues with a source density of 30 arcmin$^{-2}$ and intrinsic ellipticity dispersion $\sigma_{\epsilon}=0.3$. We constrain mass and concentration from one-dimensional NFW and BMO fits, then recover ellipticity, position angle and centre using a two-dimensional elliptical NFW model. We also measure morphology from true convergence maps, Kaiser \& Squires reconstructions and strong-lensing tangential critical lines. Results. Recovered parameters depend on orientation and dynamical state. The relaxed cluster has similar inner and large-scale shapes, whereas disturbed systems appear more elliptical centrally. Two-dimensional weak-lensing modelling recovers the projected mass orientation despite source sampling and shape noise. Kaiser \& Squires reconstructions recover the position angle well but favour rounder mass distributions. Centroid offsets are larger in unrelaxed systems. Conclusions. Combining weak- and strong-lensing morphology probes cluster structure across physical scales and offers a promising way to investigate morphology and dynamical state.

papers.title: The Stellar Populations of Resolved Galaxies
papers.abstract: The study of galaxies outside the Milky Way using observations of resolved stellar populations has experienced extraordinary growth over the past two decades. There now exist panchromatic photometry and precise astrometry for hundreds of millions of individually resolved stars in hundreds of galaxies that span $\sim10^9$ in luminosity, $\sim10^3$ in metallicity, and sample a wide range of environments. Here, we review advances in extragalactic astronomy enabled by resolved stellar population imaging. We summarize major observational programs and focus on four interconnected science areas: the star formation histories of galaxies, 'bursty' star formation, the stellar initial mass function, and the orbital histories of Local Group galaxies. We review the literature in each area, synthesize key findings, identify emerging trends, and discuss how new and future facilities (e.g., JWST, LSST, Euclid, Roman, CSST, ELTs, HWO) will enable further progress. Finally, we highlight shortcomings in current datasets and discuss promising directions for new areas of investigation.

papers.title: Detection of star formation in a near-pristine pocket of the Universe
papers.abstract: We detect two high-confidence star-forming sources in the environment of a chemically near-pristine ([Fe/H] $<-3.66~;2\sigma)$ Damped Ly$\alpha$ system (DLA) using Keck/KCWI. These are found via the hydrogen Ly$\alpha$ emission line at $\Delta v=-1200$ kms$^{-1}$ (LAE1) and $\Delta v = -200$ kms$^{-1}$ (LAE2) relative to the DLA redshift ($z_{\rm abs} = 3.078$) at an impact parameter of $b=66$ physical kpc and $b=137$ physical kpc. We measure Ly$\alpha$ fluxes of $F(\rm Ly\alpha)_{\rm LAE1} =4.4\pm 0.7\times10^{-18}~\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}$ and $F(\rm Ly\alpha)_{\rm LAE2} =3.8\pm 0.9\times10^{-18}~\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}$. This marks the first detection of star formation in the environment of a chemically near-pristine DLA. We use red channel Keck/KCRM data to place limits on the associated He II 1640 A emission flux of these sources, $F(\rm He\,II)<3.8\times10^{-19}~\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}~(3\sigma)$ and $F(\rm He\,II) <3.7\times10^{-19}~\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}~(3\sigma)$. The weak and narrow properties of the Ly$\alpha$ emission, combined with the inferred position on the mass-metallicity relation, suggest a metal-paucity of these galaxies. Future rest-frame optical observations are required to pin down the metallicity of LAE1 and LAE2 and test if chemically near-pristine DLAs can be used as a signpost to search for primitive, metal-poor galaxies 2 Gyrs after the Big Bang.

papers.title: What sets the star-formation rate in the Milky Way? I. A multi-scale view of the star-formation rate
papers.abstract: Context. The star-formation rate (SFR) is one of the key quantities that characterizes the star formation process and has been extensively investigated both observationally and theoretically. Aims. We aim to provide a coherent multi-scale view of star formation by connecting Galactic-scale conditions (kpc) to the properties of individual star-forming clumps at sub-parsec scales. Methods. We perform a set of numerical simulations with large-scale turbulent forcing designed to reproduce physical conditions typical of the solar neighbourhood. Using adaptive zooming down to 0.03 pc, we obtain a population of star-forming clumps that is analyzed and compared with observational catalogues in a companion paper. Results. For column densities and velocity dispersions consistent with Galactic values, the resulting SFR is close to the rate inferred for the Milky Way. Comparing this value with the SFR expected from pure free-fall collapse shows that turbulence provides multiscale support that lowers the SFR by more than an order of magnitude. Additional regulation by stellar feedback, including ionizing radiation and protostellar outflows, likely reduces the SFR by an additional factor of 3-10. Comparisons with observations across multiple spatial scales show good overall agreement with this model. Conclusions. These results support a picture in which turbulence plays a central role in regulating star formation in the Milky Way. In combination with stellar feedback, it limits the star formation efficiency to only a few percent. Key words. stars: formation -- ISM: clouds -- physical processes: turbulence

papers.title: Does the Escape Fraction Prescription Shape Reionization History and Morphology?
papers.abstract: The escape fraction of ionizing photons, $f_{\rm esc}$, is one of the least constrained quantities of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), and the opacity of the intergalactic medium prevents its direct measurement at high redshifts. We constrain three power-law parameterizations, $f_{\rm esc}(z)$, $f_{\rm esc}(M_{\rm h})$, and $f_{\rm esc}(z, M_{\rm h})$, against JWST UV luminosity functions and EoR observables (the ionizing emissivity, the neutral hydrogen fraction, and the Thomson optical depth) using Markov Chain Monte Carlo, with priors that allow $f_{\rm esc}$ to either increase or decrease with redshift and halo mass. We then propagate the best-fit models into the semi-numerical simulation SimFast21 and compare their ionization morphology and 21 cm power spectra with those of a constant-$f_{\rm esc}$ model. All models reproduce the observations with nearly identical global reionization histories. The data favor an escape fraction that decreases with increasing redshift, from $\approx 0.8$ at $z = 5$ to $\approx 0.35$ at $z = 15$. The halo-mass-only model prefers $f_{\rm esc}$ increasing with halo mass, but this trend acts as a proxy for redshift evolution. When we vary both dependencies jointly, the data prefer a mass-independent $f_{\rm esc}$. At matched global neutral fraction, the ionization morphology is closely similar for all four prescriptions, and the 21 cm power spectra agree to within $\approx 10\%$. These results suggest that, once calibrated against the same observations, the details of the $f_{\rm esc}$ prescription, which are set by the physics of the interstellar medium, largely average out in both the global observables and the 21 cm power spectrum. Distinguishing them may require statistics beyond the power spectrum, such as sightline statistics of the Ly$\alpha$ and 21 cm forests, or forecasts that exploit their small differences in reionization timing.

papers.title: ECH0EZ: Estimating the Hubble constant with ZTF SN Ia DR2
papers.abstract: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are instrumental for a precise measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) from the local distance ladder, yet the data used hitherto for this purpose are inhomogeneous and subject to severe selection effects. We present the first, preliminary, cosmological analysis of 772 SNe Ia from the Zwicky Transient Facility's second data release: an untargeted single-telescope sample whose volume-limited subset (z<0.06) is largely free of Malmquist bias. We correct the public data for known instrumental and calibration biases and the redshifts for peculiar motions. Using the 42 SH0ES calibrators (their host distances computed from Cepheids and geometric anchors) and a Bayesian hierarchical model of SN Ia standardisation, dust extinction, redshift and calibration uncertainties, we infer $H_0 = (71.6 \pm 1.5)$ km/s/Mpc after marginalising over deceleration with a flat prior (or $(72.3 \pm 1.1)$ km/s/Mpc if a prior on matter density from Pantheon+ is imposed), with the uncertainty dominated by the number of calibrators. We demonstrate robustness to the choice of light-curve and Milky Way dust models and to extensions of the model to include peculiar-velocity correlations, a host-mass step, and two stretch populations. These results are in agreement with previous distance-ladder measurements and $2.7\sigma$ ($4.1\sigma$) away from the value obtained from Planck data, suggesting that the resolution of the Hubble tension lies outside of SNe Ia---or the distance ladder entirely.

papers.title: Dependence of Merger-driven Star Formation and Gas-phase Metallicity Evolution on Merger Type and Stellar Mass
papers.abstract: Galaxy mergers play a fundamental role in driving gas inflows, altering star formation, and redistributing metals, yet how these processes depend on merger type, merger stage, and progenitor galaxy properties remains incompletely understood. In this work, we investigate the resolved impact of mergers on star formation rate (SFR) and gas-phase metallicity using MaNGA integral-field spectroscopy and the MaNGA Galaxy Merger Catalog of Comerford et al. (2024). By comparing merger galaxies to matched controls, we quantify local offsets in SFR and metallicity as functions of merger type, merger stage, stellar mass, and galactocentric radius. We find that major mergers generally exhibit stronger SFR enhancement and greater metallicity dilution than minor mergers. In major mergers, SFR enhancement is often spatially extended, whereas in minor mergers it is weaker and more centrally concentrated. The SFR response in major mergers varies non-monotonically with merger stage, with stronger enhancement in the early (first-passage) and post-coalescence stages and weaker enhancement in the late (between-passage) stage. Metallicity dilution is generally strongest in early-stage major mergers and weaker at later stages, although this stage dependence is not monotonic across all stellar-mass bins. We also find stellar-mass dependence that lower-mass systems show stronger metallicity dilution in both major and minor mergers, while the strongest SFR enhancement occurs in intermediate- and high-mass major mergers. These results show that the resolved star formation and metallicity responses depend jointly on merger type, merger stage, and stellar mass and exhibit different behaviors across the merger sequence.

papers.title: Prospects for Near-Far Constraints on Reionization from Simulated LSST Observations of Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies and Stellar Streams
papers.abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will detect resolved stellar populations of intact dwarf galaxies and disrupted stellar streams in the Milky Way (MW) halo and beyond, opening a new avenue for near-field cosmology, particularly for constraining the faint galaxies during reionization. To interpret these data, we present and publicly release mock LSST catalogs of satellites, stellar streams, phase-mixed galaxies, and field galaxies around 13 MW-mass hosts in the FIRE-2 zoom-in simulations, generated with \textsf{py-ananke}. Using a surface brightness limit of $\mu_{g} \leq 34$ $\rm{mag}$ $\rm{arcsec^{-2}}$, we find that $\approx29\%$ of streams with $M_{\star} \gtrsim 5 \times 10^5$ $M_{\odot}$ are detectable with tidal tails, while another $\approx38\%$ are detectable only through their bound progenitors and would appear as satellites. We estimate that $\approx96\%$ of satellites and $\approx64\%$ of field galaxies (out to $\sim$3.5 Mpc) with $M_{\star} \gtrsim 10^{5}$ $M_{\odot}$ are detectable, decreasing to $\approx$59\% and $\approx$42\% for $M_{\star} \gtrsim 10^{4.5}$ $M_{\odot}$ owing to resolution limits. Including streams detectable as satellites reproduces the radial distribution of observed MW satellites, suggesting that some observed satellites may be bound remnants of disrupted systems. Our mock galaxies match the sizes of observed satellites with $M_{\rm{V}} \lesssim -6$. Star-formation histories computed from only the detectable stars broadly recover the simulated star-formation histories. As an application, we test the near-far technique for reconstructing the proto-MW ultraviolet luminosity function (UVLF) during reionization ($z \gtrsim 6$). Adding the detectable streams improves the recovered faint-end slope at $z = 7$ and reduces the halo-to-halo scatter by $\approx33\%$.

papers.title: What sets the star-formation rate in the Milky Way?. II. Comparing the star-forming clumps from simulations and observations
papers.abstract: Context. Linking the star formation (SF) properties of dense clumps to their parent large-scale environment is a key step to interpret Galactic surveys. Achieving a consistent, multi-scale picture of SF requires a comparative analysis of observations and simulations. Aims. We exploit kiloparsec-scale magneto-hydrodynamic simulations designed to reproduce local Milky Way conditions. Leveraging the wide range of scales covered by the simulations (reaching a resolution of 0.03 pc), we aim to compare the properties of the simulated population of star-forming clumps with observational catalogues. Methods. After extracting the star-forming structures with the HOP clump-finding algorithm, we compare their physical (mass and size) and SF properties (SF rate and efficiency) with those of the Hi-GAL compact source catalogue. Results. Despite the different methodologies and the three-dimensional nature of our clump extraction, the simulated clumps show good agreement with the observed sample in their mass and size distributions. We discover a consistently linear relation between mass and SF rate (SFR) for the simulated clumps, which is remarkably independent of the initial conditions of the boxes. Using scaling relations to distinguish between turbulence- and gravity-regulated gas inflow onto the clump scales, we find tentative evidence in favour of a gravity-regulated regime of SF at the probed sub-parsec scales. Key words. methods: numerical - stars: formation - ISM: clouds

papers.title: Fresh Look at Shift Symmetric Modified Gravity
papers.abstract: Shift symmetric Horndeski gravity can be a simple, well posed theory with protection against quantum corrections. Overturning conventional thought that such a theory cannot cross the phantom divide ($w=-1$) we present both analytic and numerical proof that it can. We carry out a detailed dynamical systems analysis showing the evolution of ghost free and stable regions within the model family, identify the fixed point and dynamical attractor structure, and derive the interaction of the $w=-1$ curve with these phase space structures. This reveals two mechanisms for cosmologies crossing the phantom divide while preserving shift symmetry.

papers.title: Scalarized Einstein-Maxwell black holes in external scalar fields
papers.abstract: We construct static black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory under prescribed external scalar fields, mapping their existence domain and determining how their scalar charges vary with the external field. Focusing on solutions with positive scalar charge, we find that a positive external field induces scalar charge in Reissner-Nordström (RN) black holes below the zero-source scalarization threshold and extends the allowed charge-to-mass range. A negative external field instead introduces a finite lower existence boundary and permits distinct black holes under identical external conditions. Coupling these isolated responses through the leading companion-generated scalar fields, we find mutual scalar induction in binaries whose components are RN black holes in isolation. For binaries with scalar charges of the same sign, their scalar charges need not increase as the separation decreases, while some binaries with opposite scalar charges admit multiple equilibria and cannot continue along their original equilibrium branches to smaller separations.

papers.title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
papers.abstract: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. In many extensions of general relativity, GW propagation is modified by an anomalous friction term, which alters the amplitude evolution and leads to a GW luminosity distance that differs from its electromagnetic counterpart. In this work, we develop a non-parametric reconstruction of this anomalous friction from dark standard sirens. We reconstruct its redshift dependence, encoded in the friction function $\alpha_M(z)$, with a Gaussian process (GP) and derive the corresponding GW-to-EM luminosity-distance ratio $\Xi(z)$ by integration, explicitly retaining the relation between the local friction modification and its accumulated effect on the observed distance, while enforcing a monotonic and invertible GW luminosity distance. We apply the method to the GWTC-5.0 catalog, jointly inferring the source population, modified propagation, and background cosmological parameters. We find no evidence for departures from GR, with $\alpha_M=0$ and $\Xi=1$ consistent with the posterior over the redshift range probed by the catalog. The result is stable under variations of the GP kernel, smoothness and amplitude priors, resolution prescription, and likelihood treatment. We further introduce function-space diagnostics for comparing flexible and parametric reconstructions, including prior calibration, prior-to-posterior contraction, common summaries of propagation-population degeneracies, and principal-component analysis. These tools make explicit which features are informed by the data and which are imposed by the function-space prior, providing a framework for interpretable non-parametric tests of gravitational-wave propagation.

papers.title: The Cosmic Ultraviolet Baryon Survey X: Density and Pressure Profiles of Clumpy Circumgalactic Gas at $z=0.4-0.7$
papers.abstract: The thermodynamic state and turbulent properties of the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) are investigated for 23 galaxies and galaxy groups at intermediate redshift ($z=0.4$--0.7) in the Cosmic Ultraviolet Baryon Survey (CUBS) midz sample using background QSOs within the virial radius. Kinematically resolved absorption-line measurements from Hubble Space Telescope/COS and STIS spectra, combined with photoionization modeling, yield gas densities of $n_\mathrm{H}\approx10^{-4}$--$10^{-2} \ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$, temperatures of $T\approx(1$--$5) \times 10^4\,\mathrm{K}$, and non-thermal line broadening of $b_\mathrm{NT}\approx2$--$30 \ \mathrm{km \ s^{-1}}$ for individual cool clumps. Combined with published samples at similar redshifts, the results indicate that photoionization equilibrium accurately describes the cool CGM and that turbulent motions are predominantly subsonic. At fixed projected distance, cool-gas density decreases systematically with halo mass, while inferred cool-gas pressures in $M_h\approx10^{12}$--$10^{13}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ halos are consistent with hot-gas pressures inferred from stacked X-ray observations. The analysis uncovers a near constant total cool gas mass across a broad halo mass range, which directly translates to a declining baryon mass fraction in the cool phase from $\approx 6$--$19\%$ in halos of $M_h \approx 10^{12}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$ to $\approx 0.6$--$1.5\%$ in halos of $M_h \approx 10^{13}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$. Finally, several CUBS galaxies exhibit kinematically aligned low- and high-ionization species spanning up to two orders of magnitude in density, reflecting local fluctuations in the halo gas pressure.

papers.title: Heavy Seeds and the Multi-scale Fueling of Early Supermassive Black Holes and Little Red Dots
papers.abstract: The formation of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in the early Universe has been a longstanding mystery due to the brief period available to assemble them. More recently, the unexpected discovery with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) of Little Red Dots (LRDs), compact sources exhibiting signatures of active galactic nuclei (AGN), has accentuated this challenge. Cosmological simulations investigating their formation and evolution confront the limitation that the compact scale of SMBH/LRD physics cannot be simultaneously resolved with the larger-scale cosmological environment. We address this limitation by utilizing a cutout technique, selecting a targeted region around an SMBH seed from a cosmological parent simulation and re-running the cutout at higher (sub-pc) resolution for shorter periods. We explore two SMBH formation scenarios: the standard, light seed stellar-remnant case, and the heavy-seed, direct collapse black hole (DCBH) channel. Within the high-resolution achieved by the cutouts, the DCBH, due to its larger mass, is able to induce a buildup of high density gas nearby and accrete gas in bursts of super-Eddington phases, growing in mass and producing an LRD-like spectrum. In contrast, the stellar remnant cannot do so and remains dormant, unable to affect the nearby gas or significantly evolve by gas accretion alone. papers.title: Unified Dynamics of Black-Hole Interiors: From Geometric to Scalar-Kinetic Dominance
papers.abstract: We identify a unified dynamical picture connecting small-amplitude scalar input at the event horizon to scalar--Kasner interiors. Within boundary-supported stationary families, area contraction drives the transition from geometric to scalar kinetic dominance. For the Schwarzschild-like branch, contraction suppresses the relative curvature contribution, so the scalar kinetic term becomes dominant while the gradient remains small. For the Kerr--Newman-like branch, the scalar gradient is strongly amplified as area contraction carries the solution toward the would-be Cauchy-horizon zero, followed by a narrow transition to scalar kinetic dominance. Cancellation between the kinetic and geometric terms produces a positive minimum of a metric diagnostic, explaining inner-horizon loss dynamically. Fully coupled numerical solutions for the Schwarzschild-like branch and four-dimensional stationary axisymmetric Kerr--Newman interiors, including the Reissner--Nordström and Kerr limits, support this picture. Area contraction provides the common physical mechanism, while the would-be Cauchy-horizon zero determines the strength of gradient amplification and the localization of the transition.

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Approach to Gravitational Particle Production in the Inflation-Kination Transition: Surveying a Wide Range of the Parameter Space
papers.abstract: In this study, we investigate the gravitational particle production (GPP) as a natural reheating channel in time-dependent backgrounds. We focus on reheating in an inflation-kination background. To maintain generality across inflationary models, we use a continuous scale-factor function that produces this transition and has been proposed in the literature. In this scenario, the gravitational reheating channel arises from the gravitational excitation of a superheavy spectator scalar field with Ricci-matter gravitational coupling. Besides all the perturbative approaches, a recently proposed non-perturbative one that uses the notion of the adiabatic vacuum has also been applied to the case of superheavy particles. Although the effect of the mass of the field on the reheating temperature has been investigated, the impact of the non-conformal values of the gravitational coupling constant on the GPP rate is not considered. Hence, we modify the non-perturbative approach in such a way that both effects can be traced. Three parameters affect the reheating temperature in this case: the bare mass of the field, the gravitational coupling constant, and the transition time. In this paper, the effect of each of these parameters alone on the resultant reheating temperature, as well as the combined effects of these parameters, is studied. Taking into account all involved parameters and surveying a wide range of the 3D parameter space, the highest reheating temperature possible is obtained. All of the aforementioned investigations are done based on numerical calculations, and we obtain that the highest possible reheating temperature is quite sufficient for the universe to enter the Hot Big-Bang era. For the sake of completeness, we study the GPP in such a transition using an analytical method in an independent, parallel, solvable model. This analysis is presented only as a mathematical tool.

papers.title: The inner galaxy as a window on its early assembly: lessons from a cosmological Milky Way analogue
papers.abstract: Characterising the assembly history of the inner Milky Way is a key goal of upcoming spectroscopic surveys, yet disentangling its overlapping stellar components remains challenging. We investigate the chemodynamics of the centre of a Milky Way analogue in the Auriga Superstars cosmological hydrodynamical simulation suite, focusing on a high-resolution halo (~ 800 M_sun star particles) with a realistic galactic bar and accretion history. We classify stars within the inner 4 kpc into proto-galaxy, subsequent in-situ, and accreted components to assess their distinguishability using kinematics, dynamics, ages, and metallicities. Stellar net rotation declines sharply between [Fe/H]=0 and [Fe/H]=-1, marking the transition from disc-like in-situ stars to the proto-galaxy. While significant chemical and dynamical overlaps complicate the search for structures in energy-angular momentum (E-Lz) space, metal-poor stars ([Fe/H]<-1) at low energy form a remarkably pure (>97%) sample of proto-galaxy stars. Conversely, the high-energy, metal-poor tail offers the best chance of detecting accreted debris. However, at high energies the inner accreted halo is dominated by low-mass systems (M_star ~ 10^7 - 10^9 M _sun), not the earliest massive mergers. Dynamically, few clues remain from early mergers, and early enrichment is rapid and similar across progenitors. In-situ contamination is an issue for [Fe/H]>-1 throughout E-Lz space. Overall, while accurate stellar ages and high-precision chemical abundances may help further constrain the Milky Way's history, we should be cautious when associating stars with individual merger events in the inner galaxy.

papers.title: The Symbiosis of Vainshtein and Chameleon Screening

papers.title: Unveiling the nonthermal environments of NGC 3411 and NGC 5903 through new MeerKAT observations
papers.abstract: Galaxy groups are key laboratories for investigating the interplay between active galactic nucleus (AGN) outbursts and the dynamical processes of the intra-group medium. We aim to characterize the morphology, spectral properties, and magnetic field structure of the diffuse nonthermal radio emission in two peculiar galaxy groups, NGC 3411 and NGC 5903, selected from an originally larger sample, in order to constrain its origin and its connection with the dynamics of the intra-group medium. We present new MeerKAT UHF- and L-band observations of the two groups, complemented by archival Chandra and XMM-Newton data already analyzed in previous works. In NGC 3411, we detect extended radio emission surrounding the central AGN over scales of ~70 kpc, and resolve previously undetected arc-shaped substructures on scales of ~20-30 kpc. This extended component exhibits a relatively uniform steep spectrum ($\alpha$ ~ -1.7). We discuss possible scenarios for its origin, including mini-halos, aged AGN plasma, weak shocks, and the possibility of a radio galaxy observed along the line of sight. In NGC 5903, MeerKAT reveals a complex filamentary morphology, including a previously unknown ring-like structure surrounding the central AGN. Spectral-index mapping shows localized flattening ($\alpha$ ~ -0.9) along the north arc, while polarization data reveal ordered magnetic fields and a patchy rotation measure distribution across the source. Together with the disturbed X-ray morphology, these results support a scenario in which fossil AGN plasma has been redistributed and locally reenergized by group-scale dynamical processes such as turbulence, shear, and weak compression. Our results demonstrate that galaxy groups can host a rich variety of nonthermal phenomena, whose properties can only be fully revealed through the combination of sensitive, high-resolution, and multifrequency radio observations.

papers.title: NOCTURNE. VI. Hour-timescale radio variability in early-stage active galactic nucleus SDSS J122844.81+501751.2
papers.abstract: Recently, a sample of radio-weak active galactic nuclei (AGN) was discovered to exhibit extreme Jy-level radio flares at 37~GHz. The origin of these extraordinary flares remains unknown. All sources host low-mass supermassive black holes, and most of them can be classified as narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. We employed multiwavelength observations to investigate one of these sources, SDSS J122844.81+501751.2, during a period of high 37~GHz activity. Our data include radio observations from Metsähovi Radio Observatory (MRO) at 37~GHz, OVRO at 15~GHz, and JVLA at 15, 22, and 33~GHz, as well as optical, UV, and X-ray observations from \textit{Swift}/XRT and UVOT. We studied the variability of the multiwavelength light curves (LC) using statistical tests, as well as derived the $e$-folding timescales of the flares. Utilising the timescales and the observed flare properties, we estimated the variability brightness temperatures and Doppler factors associated with the flares. Most individual LCs do not show statistically significant variability, which is likely due to the low number of measurements. The shortest timescale we estimated is only 1.1~hours, measured between MRO 37~GHz and JVLA 33~GHz detections. This is the fastest intrinsic radio variability reported in an AGN so far. This yielded an extreme variability brightness temperature of $T_\mathrm{B}$ = 4.20 $~\times$ 10$^{18}$~K and a variability Doppler factor of 438. We discuss magnetic eruptions near the black hole as a possible explanation for the extreme radio flares, and show that both incoherent and coherent processes can produce flares at these timescales. These flares challenge our current understanding of AGN radio variability. Whereas magnetic eruptions offer a viable explanation for the flares, more observations, preferably broadband and including polarisation, will be required to confirm their origin. (abridged)

papers.title: Non-minimal $α$-attractor magnetogenesis with potential dependent couplings
papers.abstract: We investigate inflationary magnetogenesis driven by a non conformal coupling in the case of large-field $\alpha$-attractor inspired models. Our numerical results show that the non-minimal coupling affects the evolution of the electromagnetic sector and the resulting magnetic-field amplitude. We find that, within the analyzed configurations, minimally coupled and $\xi>0$ scenarios are compatible with the adopted CMB constraints, yielding conditional present-day magnetic-field estimates of order $10^{-23}$ G.

papers.title: Impact of Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus Debris on Milky Way Escape-velocity Estimates in TNG50
papers.abstract: The escape velocity is a key probe of the Milky Way (MW) potential, but standard estimates can be biased by unrelaxed substructures. Using MW analogs from the TNG50 cosmological simulation, we investigate the impact of the dominant, highly radial Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) debris on escape-velocity measurements. We introduce an adaptive selection strategy that balances statistical reliability with sample size to identify the power-law decline regime of the local halo velocity distribution. Applying this strategy to 16 MW analogs with prominent GSE-like structures and continuous high-velocity tails, we find that retaining GSE-like stars yields a systematic underestimate, with a recovery fraction of $97.5^{+2.1}_{-2.9}\%$, while removing GSE-like stars alone increases the recovery fraction to $99.4^{+2.1}_{-2.5}\%$. The $\sim 2\%$ underestimation of the escape velocity corresponds to an $\sim 6\%$ underestimation of the total mass. This improvement persists in LAMOST-like magnitude and footprint selection. GSE-like debris is therefore a key contributor to the systematic underestimation of escape-velocity measurements, with direct implications for the inferred MW mass.

papers.title: ASKAP Discovery of a Giant Odd Radio Circle at $z=0.15$
papers.abstract: Odd radio circles (ORCs) are a recently recognized class of faint, roughly circular diffuse radio sources, typically a few hundred kiloparsecs across, whose origin is still debated. It contains an AGN jet with a power-law spectrum of index $\alpha=-0.877\pm0.089$ between 856 and 1656~MHz. Finally, we discuss the implications for ORC formation models and the observations needed to establish the nature of this system.

papers.title: Towards Reliably Measuring the Mass-Size Relation of Dark Matter Halos: Impact of projection, miscentering and Eddington bias
papers.abstract: In the conventional spherical overdensity definition of a dark matter halo, masses and radii, e.g. $M_{200{\rm m}}$ and $r_{200{\rm m}}$, are equivalent. However, halos do exhibit a physical boundary at the splashback radius $r_{\rm sp}$, which manifests as a sharp drop in density. Splashback radii are now routinely measured in stacked weak lensing profiles, but the expected trend of decreasing $r_{\rm sp}/r_{200{\rm m}}$ with mass has not been verified in observed galaxy groups or clusters. In this work, we show that several observational effects conceal the predicted mass-size relation. In particular, we quantify the impact of systematics on the mean density and lensing profiles of mock-observed halo samples, which are created by applying a realistic cluster-finding procedure to dark matter-only simulations. We reproduce the known impact of projection: preferentially observing systems in overdense regions. But, differing from previous works, we show that the same projection effect, combined with scatter in observed luminosities, causes a significant Eddington bias in the derived mass-observable relation and a complex suppression in mean density profiles over all radial scales. The magnitude of this effect is mass-dependent and coupled to the cluster-finding procedure and survey properties, making it challenging to model simply and motivating full forward-modeling of observed group and cluster samples. However, we demonstrate that a simple mitigation approach, effectively a weak lensing mass calibration, does well in approximately recovering the true mass-size relation. Finally, we show that only severe miscentering can bias the measurement of the halo size, but any miscentering can increase the measurement uncertainty.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Bayesian Differential Calibration of the Gaia DR3 Parallax Zero Point Using Galactic Globular Clusters

In five-fold cross-validation that excludes entire clusters from training, the correction modestly reduces the magnitude- and color-trend RMS relative to the L21 correction. The resulting model therefore provides a differential refinement of the \textit{Gaia} DR3 parallax zero-point within the calibrated domain for GCs, rather than an independent determination of its absolute value.

papers.title: Testing Conformal Weyl Gravity with Plasma Modified Black Hole Shadows and EHT Constraints
papers.abstract: We study the shadows of a charged rotating de Sitter solution in fourth order conformal Weyl gravity (CWG) immersed in plasma and analyze the joint charge-plasma constraints. Charge ($q$) produces a stronger theory dependence: for the representative parameters studied, increasing $q$ enlarges the CWG shadow but reduces the GR shadow. The lensing behavior independently supports the geometry-dependent response found from the photon region and shadow observables. We further compare the finite observer dimensionless shadow radius with EHT-inferred size intervals for Sgr~A$^*$ and M87$^*$. Our results indicate that plasma effects can mimic part of the shadow size shift, but the distinct charge response of CWG offers a potential observational route for separating conformal gravity signatures from environmental propagation effects.

papers.title: Warm inflation beyond the Gaussian limit: primordial black holes and induced gravitational waves
papers.abstract: In warm inflation, the primordial fluctuations are driven by random kicks from a hot radiation bath. Two features of these kicks matter: how long the bath remembers them, which shapes the power spectrum, and how their strengths are spread, which controls the rare, extreme fluctuations. In this paper, we investigate how primordial black holes and the accompanying induced gravitational waves can be used to discriminate between these two features. We use a simple model inspired by warm inflation, in which independent kicks of random strength add up to a narrow peak in the power spectrum. At leading order, the induced gravitational wave depends only on the power spectrum and is therefore insensitive to how the kicks are distributed. However, the black holes are very sensitive to these rare large fluctuations. Hence, two baths can yield the same gravitational wave signal while forming black holes at very different rates. A modest kurtosis range of 0.1 to 0.3 enhances black-hole formation by factors of ten to a million at fixed gravitational-wave amplitude, the larger factors for the rarer black holes. Counting peaks rather than all points, or widening the spectrum, lowers the enhancement by at most a factor of about four. In general a change in the power affects both phenomena, while the kurtosis affects only the black hole production.

In this work, we consider two parity-even cubic-curvature couplings and one quartic-curvature coupling, whose leading phase corrections enter at 5PN, 6PN, and 8PN order, respectively. We incorporate these corrections into the individual multipoles of the \texttt{SEOBNRv5HM\_ROM} waveform using the flexible theory-independent framework, allowing higher-order modes and the full inspiral-merger-ringdown signal to be used in the analysis. The posterior distributions are consistent with GR, with all three couplings consistent with zero at 90\% credibility. papers.title: Impact of deformation parameters on the greybody factor and Joule-Thomson expansions of Schwarzschild-AdS black hole
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the greybody factor and Joule-Thomson expansion of deformed Schwarzschild-AdS black hole models. We constructed the Klein-Gordon equation into a Schrödinger-like wave equation using tortoise coordinates and derived the exact effective potential. Also, we analyzed its behavior under varying physical parameters, including deformation parameters, mass and angular momentum. In this case, our results illustrate that increasing the deformation parameter enhances the effective potential, significantly impacting the absorption and scattering of massless scalar fields. It is noted that the Schwarzschild black hole effective potential is greatly increased when the deformation parameter is present. Near the event horizon, we found that waves behave differently, with higher-frequency waves more easily penetrating potential obstacles and lower-frequency waves bouncing off them. Furthermore, we investigated the thermodynamic characteristics of black holes using the Joule-Thomson expansion, detecting isenthalpic curves that indicate heating and cooling zones controlled by pressure and temperature changes. In this context, we tested the influence of deformation black hole parameters; the isenthalpic curves are enhanced by increasing the deformation parameters and the black hole mass.

papers.title: Relativistic N-body simulations with mass-varying neutrinos
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological data provide weak hints for smaller masses than what is required by neutrino-oscillation experiments, motivating investigations into variation of the neutrino masses with cosmic time. Here we study a model where the neutrinos couple to a quintessence field that acts as dark energy. We compute structure formation using fully dynamical and relativistic N-body and lattice simulations, with nonlinear field evolution and a weak-field metric expansion. Similar to previous studies, we find the generic appearance of neutrino lumps, but observe them to be highly dynamical and spinning. We study several models where the effective dark energy, including nonlinear effects of the scalar field on the cosmic expansion, can show phantom crossing. The relativistic physics available in our simulation framework can help distinguish such models from LCDM, through observations of neutrino and dark energy properties, and slip between the gravitational potentials due to anisotropic stress. The rich phenomenology offered by mass-varying neutrinos motivates further exploration and development of the simulation techniques.

papers.title: Novel topological subclasses of a magnetic black hole in causal nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract: By treating black-hole states as topological defects in thermodynamic parameter space, we investigate a static, asymptotically flat magnetic black holes in Einstein gravity coupled to causal nonlinear electrodynamics. Using the generalized off-shell free energy and Duan's $\phi$-mapping topological current theory, we analyze the physical single-horizon sector in the canonical ensemble. We identify four representative defect-curve profiles, including realizations of the conjectured $W^{0+\leftrightarrow1-}$ class and $\overline{W}^{1-}$ subclass, as well as a new thermodynamic topological subclass, $\overline{W}^{0+\leftrightarrow1-}$. This new subclass features paired generation and annihilation points, with unstable innermost and outermost branches. As the auxiliary inverse temperature increases, the system evolves from two equilibrium states to three and then back to one, with an unstable small-black-hole defect entering through the physical lower boundary and changing the global topological number from $W=0$ to $W=-1$. This boundary-induced change signals a thermodynamic topological phase transition. These results show that the same inverse-temperature endpoint behavior and winding-number sequence from small to large black holes can accompany different defect evolution, highlighting the role of the physical horizon boundary in thermodynamic topological classification. More broadly, this causal nonlinear-electrodynamics black-hole family provides a setting for discovering further defect structures and thermodynamic topological phase transitions.

papers.title: Realistic neutron stars in the constant-Q branch of f(Q) gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the hydrostatic equilibrium and global structure of neutron stars within symmetric teleparallel gravity, where gravitational interactions are mediated by the non-metricity scalar $Q$. Working within the metric-affine formulation, we adopt the regular, constant-$Q$ branch ($Q = Q_*$) of $f(Q)$ gravity, which preserves regularity at the stellar centre while maintaining explicit dependence on the non-linear functional form through $f(Q_*)$ and its derivatives. We propose three novel non-linear $f(Q)$ extensions: (i) a Born-Infeld-inspired model, (ii) a Hu--Sawicki analogue, and (iii) a Tsujikawa-inspired model. Incorporating state-of-the-art realistic unified equations of state, namely GPPVA(DD2) and SLy4, we numerically solve the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and evaluate stellar stability via the Harrison-Zel'dovich-Novikov criterion. The Born-Infeld and Hu-Sawicki analogues smoothly recover the general relativistic limit as their control parameters increase, predicting stellar radii for low-mass objects ($M < 2.0\,M_\odot$) that match observational constraints from X-ray binaries and GW170817; however, their maximum masses remain capped below $2.43\,M_\odot$ (DD2) and $2.06\,M_\odot$ (SLy4). Conversely, the Tsujikawa-inspired model significantly stiffens the effective gravitational coupling, accommodating massive compact objects up to $\sim 3.36\,M_\odot$ and offering a viable physical origin for the $2.59_{-0.09}^{+0.08}\,M_\odot$ secondary object in GW190814, albeit at the expense of overpredicting radii for typical low-mass neutron stars. These contrasting behaviours demonstrate a key phenomenological complementarity between maximum mass and radius bounds within the constant-$Q$ framework, highlighting the utility of multimessenger observations in constraining non-linear non-metricity gravity.

papers.title: Primordial black holes from a type-IIB/F theory inflaton potential
papers.abstract: We study the possibility of the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs) using an inflaton potential constructed by stabilizing all Kähler moduli employing both the perturbative and non-perturbative corrections in the large volume scenario in type-IIB/F string theory. We further introduce a small perturbation in one of the Kähler moduli that modifies the existing potential in the field space. The effective correction in the moduli space is made by introducing a localised Gaussian bump, which induces an ultra-slow-roll feature in the inflaton potential during the early cosmological inflation. The evolution of the amplitude of the curvature power spectrum is solved numerically by using the Mukhanov-Sasaki equation, with Bunch-Davies initial conditions. The inclusion of the Gaussian bump produces a sustainable enhancement in the amplitude of curvature power spectra around $k\sim 1.12 \times 10^{9} Mpc^{-1}$ for the formation of PBHs. The abundance of PBHs ($f_{PBH}$) is calculated using the Press-Schechter formalism for different values of critical density contrast and presented in the background of contemporary $f_{PBH}$ bounds and checked for viability with existing microlensing bounds, corresponding to a mass value $10^{-6}M_\odot$ for $\delta$ threshold value $\delta_c=0.439$. The Hawking temperature and evaporation time are also determined for these black holes and found to be of the order of $2.78\times 10^{-15}$ GeV and $8.5\times10^{38}$ Gyr, respectively. The enhancement of curvature power spectra lies in the sensitivity region of the SKA observations, suggesting an indication that scalar-induced gravity waves may be probed in future observations.

papers.title: Topological Centrality in Gaia Open Clusters
papers.abstract: Open clusters exhibit diverse spatial structures that provide insight into their formation and dynamical evolution. We investigate the relationship between stellar mass segregation, network topology, and dynamical age in 871 dynamically unevolved open clusters ($\tau = t/t_{\rm rh} \leq 1$) from Gaia-based catalogs. We construct three-dimensional k-nearest-neighbor graphs and measure Degree Centrality (DC), Closeness Centrality (CL), and Betweenness Centrality (BC). For each measure, we define a network-based mass segregation ratio (MSR) by comparing the mean centrality of the most massive stars with that of all cluster members. We test the stability of these measures across connectivity parameters $k=5$--20 and compare them with the classical 3D MSR, $\Lambda_{\rm MSR,3D}$, and dynamical age. All three network ratios show positive correlations with $\Lambda_{\rm MSR,3D}$, strongest for closeness centrality, while their correlations with dynamical age are weak. These results demonstrate that network analysis provides a complementary approach to studying stellar structure and mass segregation in open clusters.

papers.title: Self-gravitating Schrödinger--Poisson Solitons in Curved Spacetime
papers.abstract: We formulate a description of self-gravitating Schrödinger--Poisson (SP) solitons in curved spacetime using a local inertial frame centered on the soliton. In the weak-field and non-relativistic regime, the effect of the background spacetime is incorporated into the SP equations through an effective tidal potential determined by the spacetime curvature. We apply this framework to a soliton moving along a circular equatorial geodesic around a Kerr black hole. The tidal field contains stationary and time-dependent quadrupolar components, which induce a deformation of the soliton and an associated mass quadrupole moment. We formulate the quadrupolar response in terms of the tidal deformability and the dimensionless Love number. We then estimate the gravitational radiation associated with the rotating deformed soliton and evaluate the corresponding characteristic strain for representative soliton sizes and orbital radii. A comparison with representative sensitivity curves of planned space-based gravitational-wave detectors identifies parameter regimes in which the estimated characteristic strain may lie within their sensitivity ranges. Our framework provides a systematic basis for investigating the tidal response of self-gravitating bosonic solitons in black-hole spacetimes and their potential gravitational-wave signatures.

papers.title: Can One Hear the Absence of a Singularity?
papers.abstract: One of the central expectations of quantum gravity is the resolution of the curvature singularities predicted by General Relativity, potentially giving rise to effective black-hole geometries that are regular inside the horizon. We show that, for a very broad class of regular black holes including several known solutions, the quasinormal-mode spectrum in the large-overtone limit differs discontinuously from that of a Schwarzschild black hole, even when the regularization parameter is arbitrarily small. The real part of the quasinormal frequencies vanishes asymptotically, rather than approaching a nonzero constant, as generically occurs in General Relativity and other theories predicting black holes with curvature singularities. The asymptotic black-hole spectrum thus retains a distinctive imprint of singularity resolution. We establish these results analytically through a systematic formulation of the monodromy method and confirm them numerically. We interpret this phenomenon as a manifestation of black-hole spectral instability, whereby arbitrarily small deviations from vacuum General Relativity produce nonperturbative changes in the large-overtone spectrum.

papers.title: Genesis in Minimally Modified Gravity
papers.abstract: We construct a Genesis scenario within the framework of a type-II minimally modified gravity. The background solution is past geodesically complete and approaches Minkowski spacetime in the asymptotic past. While the Hubble expansion rate grows, the matter sector satisfies the null-energy condition. Scalar perturbations are ghost-free and have no ultraviolet gradient instability, although the squared sound speed $c_\mathcal{R}^2$ becomes negative within a finite infrared region in the Fourier space for a finite time interval. Numerical evolution, including superhorizon growth, yields a nearly scale-invariant, slightly red-tilted scalar spectrum over a broad region of parameter space. The tensor spectrum is blue, with a strongly suppressed tensor-to-scalar ratio. Finally, using the matter fluctuation $\delta\chi$, whose asymptotic normalization is regular, we find that the background-dependent cubic couplings vanish in the far past at fixed nonzero momenta. The surviving matter--graviton and graviton self-interactions are Planck suppressed.

papers.title: Thermodynamics and phase structure of rotating Hayward-AdS black holes
papers.abstract: We use the modified Newman--Janis algorithm to obtain the rotating ``mother'' black hole solution of the rotating Hayward-AdS black hole. We further derive the fundamental thermodynamic quantities of the ``mother'' black hole in the full unconstrained phase space $(S,J,q,\alpha,P)$, and impose the regularity condition $M_1=q^3/\alpha$ to obtain the thermodynamic quantities of the rotating Hayward-AdS regular black hole. This order of operations gives a Hawking temperature identical to the surface gravity temperature and produces the correct response functions of the regular black hole. For $P<P_c$, the Hawking temperature $T_2$ possesses a local maximum and a local minimum, which divides the black hole into small, intermediate, and large black hole branches, and the $P$--$V$ isotherms display oscillatory behavior characteristic of a liquid/gas phase transition. The small and large black hole branches are locally stable, whereas the intermediate black hole branch has negative heat capacity and is locally unstable. Increasing the rotation parameter $a$, magnetic charge $q$, or pressure $P$ reduces the region of the intermediate branch. The $G_2$--$T_2$ diagram shows that the phase structure, in contrast to the standard swallowtail of the Reissner--Nordström-AdS and Kerr--Newman-AdS black holes, is 8-shaped or C-shaped. These two shapes are divided by the characteristic pressure $P_z$. For $P<P_z$, the curve is 8-shaped, corresponding to a first-order small/large black hole transition. For $P_z<P<P_c$, the curve is C-shaped, corresponding to a zeroth-order transition. These results show that the 8-shaped/C-shaped phase structure characteristic of regular AdS black holes persists under rotation, indicating that it stems from the restructuring of the thermodynamic phase space by the regularity condition rather than from spherical symmetry.

papers.title: Rare Blue-core BCGs as Optical Signatures of ICM Cooling
papers.abstract: Blue cores in brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) trace recent central activity associated with cooling cluster atmospheres. We search for blue cores at $z<0.6$ in five eROSITA all-sky surveys using X-ray data, optical imaging, and optical spectroscopy. We identify 379 blue-core BCGs among 11352 systems (3.3%), although contamination increases toward higher redshift. Of these, 98 (0.86%) are X-ray bright. Their defining signature is a central $g-r$ color at least 0.2 mag bluer than the reference population within $a=20$ kpc before returning to the normal BCG envelope. Ha emission equivalent width correlates strongly with the blue continuum excess, consistent with young stellar components comprising ~0.1-1% of pre-existing stellar mass. Line ratios indicate widespread LINER-like excitation, with a larger star-forming contribution in blue Ha emitters but substantial non-stellar excitation. This activity is closely linked to the thermodynamics of the host-cluster gas. At $0.1R_{500}$, cooling times decrease from BCGs without significant Ha emission to red and then blue Ha emitters. Blue BCGs preferentially occur in clusters with $L_{\rm X,300}>10^{44}$ erg s$^{-1}$; red Ha emitters also favor higher X-ray luminosities. The blue-core fraction rises with optical richness. For systems with $t_{\rm cool}(0.1R_{500})<20$ Gyr, doubling richness increases the odds of hosting a blue-core BCG by $2.45\pm0.39$. This indicates that cluster scale carries information beyond cooling time, plausibly through the amount of gas available for cooling and condensation. The scarcity of blue BCGs without significant Ha emission disfavors isolated short bursts followed by long Ha-quiet fading phases. It can instead be explained by sustained or closely recurrent star formation over timescales much longer than 100 Myr, or by Ha persisting through additional excitation mechanisms as the young stellar component fades.

papers.title: Noether Symmetries in Scalar--Vector--Two-Form Cosmology with a Topological BF Interaction
papers.abstract: We study a canonical scalar field coupled to isotropic triplets of Abelian one-forms and two-forms through scalar-dependent kinetic functions and a constant topological $BF$ interaction. By retaining the lapse in the homogeneous reduction, we recover the Friedmann constraint and identify a sufficient domain in which all twelve physical modes have positive kinetic terms and luminal high-frequency propagation. A separate exponential model admits an accelerating mixed solution with $a\propto t^2$, nonzero asymptotic form fractions, and bounded normalized linear perturbations. For the Noether analysis, we choose a quadratic effective potential in flat minisuperspace coordinates and solve the zero-boundary determining equations. The canonical scalar potential is hyperbolic-squared or exponential, rather than a power law in the scalar field. The causal character of the potential coordinate separates three branches: Branch I admits a de Sitter limit, Branch II cannot sustain acceleration on regular future-complete expanding trajectories, and Branch III gives an exact solution with both form sectors active and late expansion $a\propto t^{4/3}$. Comparisons with consistent uncoupled and reduced-field limits separate the form contributions from the scalar-driven acceleration. The $BF$ term changes the finite-time exchange between the form sectors but supplies no direct negative-pressure source.

papers.title: Simulations agree: the Milky Way's satellites are disrupting
papers.abstract: Recent analyses of simulated Milky Way-mass galaxies have highlighted the prevalence of satellites undergoing tidal disruption. However, these have focused on single hydrodynamical codes with a number of limitations, making it unclear how generic this result is. We compare satellite disruption in four models: two cosmological hydrodynamical simulations (Auriga and FIRE), cosmological $N$-body simulations with stellar particle tagging (Aquarius), and a semi-analytic model with varying host disk properties (SatGen). For all systems, we compute the fraction of stellar mass retained by the progenitor ($f_\text{bound}$) at the present day. We find a remarkable agreement between FIRE, Aquarius, and SatGen; all predict that $\sim$20 to 30 per cent of classical-mass satellites have $f_\text{bound} < 0.9$ ($\sim$5 to 10 per cent have $f_\text{bound} < 0.5$). Satellites in Auriga experience substantially more mass loss than other simulations, which we attribute to their massive central galaxies and large satellite sizes prior to infall. In the ultra-faint regime captured by Aquarius and SatGen, disruption rates are comparable to or exceeding those for classical satellites. The ubiquity of mass loss across models presents both an exciting opportunity (a plethora of stellar streams awaiting discovery) and a nuisance (for theorists using satellite counts to constrain dark matter).

papers.title: Geodesic dynamics and tidal forces in a quantum-regularized black hole from string T-duality
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the geodesic dynamics and tidal force effects in neutral and electrically charged regular spacetimes inspired by T-duality. We first analyze the geometric properties of these solutions, including their regular central structure and horizon configurations, and show how the interplay between the T-duality scale $\ell_0$ and the electric charge $Q$ determines the transition between black hole and horizonless geometries. We then study the motion of massive and massless particles through the corresponding effective potentials, examining the existence and stability of circular orbits and the behavior of their characteristic radii. We further investigate the tidal forces experienced by observers in radial free fall, focusing on the behavior of the radial and angular components, their extrema and sign changes, and the location of these characteristic points relative to the horizon structure of the geometry. We show that the T-duality regularization renders the tidal forces finite in the central region and gives rise to different stretching and compression regimes, including a region of simultaneous compression in both the radial and angular directions, while the electric charge modifies the strength and location of these tidal features. Finally, we analyze the evolution of the geodesic deviation vector for two sets of initial conditions. We find that both the T-duality scale and the electric charge tend to suppress the accumulated radial stretching, whereas the angular deformation is considerably less sensitive to the charge. These results show how the quantum regularization induced by T-duality and the presence of electric charge modify the orbital dynamics and tidal response of these geometries in the strong-field regime. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the corresponding classical limits are recovered appropriately.

papers.title: A Large Diversity in the Quiescent Fractions of Massive Galaxies in Proto-clusters at $z\sim4-6$ in the FRESCO GOODS fields
papers.abstract: To constrain the emergence of the first quiescent galaxies (QGs) and their connection to large-scale structure, we search for rare, high-redshift QGs in proto-clusters using spectral energy distribution modeling, multiple rest-frame color diagnostics, and visual inspection. Our sample includes 12 QG candidates with stellar masses log(M*/Msun) ~ 9-11 in four proto-clusters at z ~ 4-6 within GOODS-North (GOODS-N) and GOODS-South (GOODS-S). The selection uses 11 NIRCam filters in GOODS-N and 17 NIRCam plus 2 MIRI filters in GOODS-S, combined with 9 ancillary HST filters, covering 0.4-7.7 microns. We measure an increasing quiescent fraction with stellar mass, with averages of 1.0%(+0.7/-0.4; 5/502), 3.5%(+2.8/-1.7; 4/115), and 33.3%(+22.2/-17.5; 3/9) for log(M*/Msun) = 9 - 9.75, 9.75 - 10.5, 10.5 - 11.25, respectively, across four proto-clusters. Notably, the two GOODS-N proto-clusters at z=4.406 and z=5.194 have a quiescent fraction of 100% (2/2 at z=4.406; 1/1 at z=5.194) in their highest mass bin (log(M*/Msun) > 10.5), whereas the proto-clusters in GOODS-S at similar redshifts have zero massive quiescent galaxies. Contrary to the expectation that massive galaxies occupy cluster centers at z~0, our QGs are found primarily on the outskirts of overdensity peaks. We also find fewer robust QGs at z>5 (1/8) and none in the z=5.384 proto-cluster, consistent with simulations suggesting that efficient quenching mechanisms had not yet matured. Our results highlight the pronounced variations in quiescent fractions across proto-clusters at z>4. The emerging diversity of proto-cluster QG populations calls for a stronger understanding of the role of environment in early galaxy evolution.

papers.title: The CGM in a New Light: Emitted H$α$, [NII], and [OIII] around Simulated Dwarf Galaxies
papers.abstract: Mapping the circumgalactic medium (CGM) in emission is a critical next step in understanding its role in the baryon cycle and galaxy evolution, and dwarf galaxies ($M_{\star}\lesssim 10^9 M_{\odot}$) are essential laboratories to study the effects of feedback on the CGM. Using the Marvelous Massive Dwarfs simulation suite, we model the CGM surface brightness (SB) around dwarf galaxies in H$\alpha$, [NII]$\lambda$6583, and [OIII]$\lambda$5007, lines accessible to current integral-field spectrographs (e.g., MUSE and KCWI) and to narrow-band imaging with the MOTHRA telephoto array. We investigate trends in SB magnitude, extent, and geometry as well as correlations with gas kinematics, recent star formation, and galaxy size. Emission in the three lines typically traces distinct CGM structures and phases. SB and the size of the emitting region can differ significantly at a given galaxy mass, but enhancements or suppression in either brightness or extent correlate well across lines. Typically, emission is preferentially eccentric and oriented along the galaxy's semi-minor axis. While outflows are key drivers in dispersing metals into the CGM and shaping SB, they remain difficult to identify in SB maps and contribute $\sim40\%$ of the total SB across lines and galaxy masses, while inflows contribute $\sim50\%$. Finally, we identify evidence for a positive correlation between SB and recent star formation and weaker but still significant evidence for a negative correlation between SB and HI disk size. These results link CGM emission to both a galaxy's recent star formation and its cumulative evolution, yielding predictions that ongoing surveys can test and further establishing emission mapping as a new window into the baryon cycle.

papers.title: Cosmological constraints on single-field inflation models from ACT/SPT data and observations at sub-Mpc scales
papers.abstract: We investigate single-field inflation models that can produce large curvature perturbations at sub-Mpc scales while remaining consistent with cosmological observations across multiple regimes. In addition, we examine the primordial power spectra predicted by these models and constrain their parameter spaces using cosmological observations at different scales, including CMB, BAO, PBH, PTA, and CMB-distortion. Our results show that some of the models considered can simultaneously satisfy the ACT/SPT constraints and account for the current PTA observations, although doing so while respecting the constraints on the PBH abundance remains challenging.

papers.title: How common are extreme scattering events?: First large sample from the ASKAP VAST survey
papers.abstract: Compact radio sources are occasionally observed to undergo extreme scattering events (ESEs): large, chromatic flux-density variations, often by more than a factor of two, over a few months. These were interpreted to be a smooth plasma lensing phenomenon due to AU-scale structures in the ISM. Although ESEs were discovered decades ago, observationally, only a few tens of ESEs have been reported, often from individual sources monitored at very high cadences. As such, the nature of the plasma lenses generating such events remains elusive. In this article, we present the most comprehensive sample of ESEs to date, using the ASKAP Variables and Slow Transients (VAST) survey. We report the discovery of a three-tier sample --- 72 sources that show promising ESE events (gold), 76 sources that are likely ESE-exhibiting (silver), and an additional 88 sources where ESE events are one plausible explanation (bronze). We show that the light curves demonstrate varied morphologies, which can be interpreted in terms of the source size and the strength of the lens in the paradigm of a simple one-dimensional Gaussian lens model. The spatial distribution of ESEs shows an appreciable excess in the direction of the Galactic center and along the Galactic loops. Using this sample, we infer an overall rate of 0.012 such events per year per deg^2 (or 0.006 events per source per year) for our (gold+silver) sample, for sources with mean flux density above 5 mJy at 888 MHz (0.01% of all isolated point sources detected in VAST).

papers.abstract: Microlensing of strongly lensed quasars probes unresolved accretion disks, but many inference methods use static magnification maps with fixed relative microlens positions. Using the GPU-accelerated simulator Microcaustics, we generate ten-year multiband light curves for three quadruply lensed quasar configurations. We compare dynamical microlensing with independent microlens motions against coherent bulk motion, and a microlens mass distribution against equal masses, keeping the velocity distribution of individual microlenses and mean mass fixed. We infer population disk sizes using ridge regression on the means and lower and upper scatters of ten variability and event metrics. We measure biases by applying models trained with simplified physics to simulations including both effects. Models trained on coherent motion interpret the additional variability from evolving caustics as smaller disks. For populations of 128 independent realizations, jointly inferred radii are consistently smaller by 6-28%. Microlens dynamics increase caustic-crossing rates pooled across all four macroimages by 5-15% and r-band high-magnification-event (HME) rates by 13-25%, while shortening median HME durations by 4-12%. Omitting the mass distribution produces configuration-dependent disk-size offsets from -12% to +5%. Including the mass distribution decreases caustic-crossing rates by 6-8% and HME rates by 6-12%. It also narrows the spread of ten-year averaged microlensing time-delay differences between macroimages by a median of 9-12% per system, while microlens dynamics have a smaller, image-pair-dependent effect. These results demonstrate the importance of microlens dynamics for population disk-size inference and motivate simulations that include dynamical microlensing and a microlens mass distribution.

papers.title: Variable Stars in Local Group Galaxies IX: Tracing the Complex History of NGC 205
papers.abstract: We present the most extensive catalogue of variable stars in NGC 205 to date, based on archival HST/ACS imaging of a single field $\sim 4^\prime$ from the galaxy centre (GO-15902). We detect 1441 RR Lyrae stars (1064 RRab, 363 RRc, and 14 of uncertain mode) and 35 anomalous Cepheids, and measure their periods, amplitudes, and intensity-mean magnitudes in the F606W and F814W bands. The variable population is dominated by RR Lyrae stars, as expected for a predominantly old (>10 Gyr) field with no strong young component. From the red giant branch tip we derive a distance modulus of $\mu = 24.68 \pm 0.06$ mag. The distribution of the RR Lyrae stars in the Bailey diagram, the fraction of RRc stars, and the presence of a substantial population of high-amplitude short-period RRab stars, indicate a range of metallicities extending to a metal-rich component, while the ratio of RR Lyrae stars to red giant branch stars indicates an extended star formation history, with only a modest fraction of the stellar mass formed in the first few Gyr. The anomalous Cepheids place NGC 205 among the slow evolvers on the relation between their frequency and host luminosity, and comparison with evolutionary models constrains their progenitors to $[\mathrm{Fe/H}] \lesssim -2.1$, indicating that metal-poor gas remained available well after the galaxy had begun to enrich. In a forthcoming paper, we will use the RR Lyrae periods and intensity-mean magnitudes to derive individual metallicities for these stars and trace the chemical enrichment history of NGC 205.
